The 28-year-old with PCOS and iron deficiency anemia returns for prenatal care of pregnancy with fetal gastroschisis. She reports a 5-day history of sharp, intermittent right-sided lower abdominal and pelvic pain that worsens with sudden movements and when changing positions, and that the pain sometimes radiates to her right groin and vaginal area.
The clinician suspects that her symptoms are due to stretching of a specific pelvic structure associated with the expanding uterus.
